merger_name: IKEA Australia – IP rights from Inter IKEA under new franchise agreement package
merger_description:
Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (**Inter IKEA**) is the worldwide IKEA franchisor and the owner of the intellectual property rights in the IKEA Concept. Inter IKEA is part of Inter IKEA Group. The holding company of Inter IKEA Group is Inter IKEA Holding B.V..

IKEA Pty Limited (**IKEA Australia**) is an Australian private company that operates the IKEA retail business in Australia. It forms part of Ingka Group, which is the largest IKEA franchisee globally. The holding company of Ingka Group is Ingka Holding B.V.. As a member of Ingka Group, IKEA Australia operates independently from Inter IKEA Group and conducts its activities under franchise agreements with Inter IKEA.

Inter IKEA’s franchise model has historically been organised on a sales-channel basis, with a separate franchise agreement for each IKEA sales channel. Inter IKEA and IKEA Australia have agreed to move to a single, consolidated franchising arrangement, under which the development and operation of all IKEA sales channels in Australia will be governed by jurisdiction-level master agreements, with each new sales channel documented through a short standard-form certificate. The new arrangement is intended to establish a clear, modern and consistent franchise framework that reflects IKEA's omni-channel approach, and to reduce the administrative burden of managing multiple channel-specific agreements. This restructuring forms part of a broader global initiative to simplify Inter IKEA's franchising agreements, with similar changes being implemented across all jurisdictions in which Inter IKEA operates.

determination_table_content.details:
Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (Inter IKEA) applied for a notification waiver
in respect of IKEA Pty Limited (IKEA Australia) proposed acquisition
of intellectual property rights under new franchise agreements
between IKEA Australia and Inter IKEA, as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).
Historically, the IKEA franchise model has been sales channel-based:
Inter IKEA enters into a separate franchise agreement for each
individual IKEA sales channel (for example, one agreement per IKEA
store).
Inter IKEA has developed a new, standardised franchise framework
that, at its core, are two master agreements:
1. the Franchise Development Agreement (FDA), governing the
development rights and obligations across a jurisdiction; and
2. the Franchise Operating Agreement (FOA), governing the
rules for development and operation of an IKEA Retail
Business in a jurisdiction.
Together, the FDA and FOA constitute the New Franchise Agreement
Package (NFAP) and cover the development and operation of an
IKEA Retail Business in a given jurisdiction under a single, consistent
set of terms. Inter IKEA proposes to terminate the existing
agreements and replace them with the Australian NFAP with IKEA
Australia.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, IKEA Australia, is an Australian private company that
operates the IKEA retail business in Australia. It forms part of Ingka
Group, which is the largest IKEA franchisee globally. The holding
company of Ingka Group is Ingka Holding B.V.. As a member of
Ingka Group, IKEA Australia operates independently from Inter IKEA
Group and conducts its activities under franchise agreements with
Inter IKEA.
The target, Inter IKEA, is the worldwide IKEA franchisor and the
owner of the intellectual property rights in the IKEA Concept. Inter
IKEA is part of Inter IKEA Group. The holding company of Inter IKEA
Group is Inter IKEA Holding B.V..

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. the Acquisition involves a restructuring of an existing
franchise relationship between Inter IKEA and IKEA Australia,
and does not change the substance of the existing franchise
relationship (including the rights to intellectual property)
b. there is no horizontal consolidation or removal of a
competitor as a result of the Acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
